newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico GDP rise surprisingly strong.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico GDP rise surprisingly strong.

text.p: Mexico reported on Wednesday an increase in gross domestic product of 7.6 percent for the fourth quarter compared to the same period a year earlier and a 5.1 percent increase for the full-year 1996.
The following are comments on the GDP rise:

"It was surprising and excellent," said Bancomer economist Carlos Rosales. "The only thing it could have been is there must have been an additional spectacular leap, possibly in the services or in the agriculture sectors," he said.
"It will mean a stronger base for comparison next year. The recovery is stronger than we thought."
Brokerage house Interacciones economist Alonso Cervera said:

"I think that the 5.1 figure for the year as a whole was somewhat expected given strong industrial production figures for fourth quarter. More surprising was the strength in fourth quarter GDP. There must have been some revisions of prior reports to arrive at 5.1 for the full year, otherwise the numbers don't add up," he said.

"The recovery has certainly been much faster than anyone would've thought a year ago. Now the challenge is to keep the rate at five percent or higher. There will be more challenges ahead particularly when there is not such low base of comparison as in 1996, as the 1995 drop allowed for an arithmetic rebound. That's a main challenge," Cervera said.
Nomura Research economist James Nash said:
"They were very good numbers, and higher than expected for the fourth quarter. GDP ended the year on a very strong note," he said.
He added that the strong growth may moderate a bit during the the year.
